Zinc Guide

Overview

This guide covers the current Zinc core: lifecycle, routing, middleware, request binding, response helpers, files, and the extension points available through Config.

App Lifecycle

zinc.New() uses the default configuration. zinc.NewWithConfig() lets you customize routing behavior, timeouts, body limits, proxy trust, rendering, validation, and error handling. 

app := zinc.New()

app.Get("/ping", func(c *zinc.Context) error {
    return c.String("pong")
})

if err := app.Listen(":8080"); err != nil {
    log.Fatal(err)
}

If you already manage listeners yourself, Zinc also supports listener-based startup and graceful shutdown. 

ln, err := net.Listen("tcp", "127.0.0.1:8080")
if err != nil {
    return err
}

go func() {
    _ = app.Serve(ln)
}()

ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 5*time.Second)
defer cancel()

if err := app.Shutdown(ctx); err != nil {
    return err
}

Routing

Zinc supports the standard HTTP methods, path parameters, wildcards, grouped routes, and helpers for matching many methods to one handler. 

app.Get("/health", func(c *zinc.Context) error {
    return c.String("ok")
})

app.Post("/users", createUser)
app.Put("/users/:id", updateUser)
app.Delete("/users/:id", deleteUser)

app.Get("/users/:id", func(c *zinc.Context) error {
    return c.JSON(zinc.Map{
        "id": c.Param("id"),
    })
})

app.Get("/files/*path", func(c *zinc.Context) error {
    return c.String(c.Param("*"))
})

app.Match([]string{zinc.MethodGet, zinc.MethodPost}, "/session", sessionHandler)
app.All("/debug", debugHandler)
app.Any("/proxy", proxyHandler)

Matched route metadata is available during the request: 

app.Get("/users/:id", func(c *zinc.Context) error {
    return c.JSON(zinc.Map{
        "full_path": c.FullPath(),
        "route":     c.Route(),
    })
})

Groups And Route Trees

Use Group for reusable prefixes and middleware. Use Route when you want inline setup without creating another named variable. 

api := app.Group("/api")
api.Get("/users", listUsers)

v1 := api.Group("/v1", authMiddleware)
v1.Get("/users/:id", showUser)

app.Route("/admin", func(admin *zinc.Group) {
    admin.Use(authMiddleware)
    admin.Get("/stats", showStats)
    admin.Get("/users", listAdminUsers)
})

Middleware

Middleware uses the same handler shape as routes. Global middleware is registered with Use; prefix-specific middleware is registered with UsePrefix. 

func requestLogger(c *zinc.Context) error {
    started := time.Now()
    err := c.Next()
    log.Printf("%s %s in %s", c.Method(), c.Path(), time.Since(started))
    return err
}

app.Use(requestLogger)

app.UsePrefix("/api", func(c *zinc.Context) error {
    c.Set("is-api", true)
    return c.Next()
})

app.Get("/private", authMiddleware, privateHandler)

If middleware returns without calling c.Next(), the chain stops. That makes early exits for auth, rate limiting, or request shaping straightforward.

Context Helpers

Context wraps the current request and response with small convenience helpers while keeping the raw *http.Request and http.ResponseWriter available. 

app.Get("/meta/:id", func(c *zinc.Context) error {
    c.Set("seen", true)
    seen, _ := c.Get("seen")

    return c.JSON(zinc.Map{
        "id":         c.Param("id"),
        "page":       c.Query("page"),
        "request_id": c.RequestID(),
        "scheme":     c.Scheme(),
        "ip":         c.IP(),
        "remote_ip":  c.RemoteIP(),
        "full_path":  c.FullPath(),
        "route":      c.Route(),
        "seen":       seen,
    })
})

Useful helpers include BodyBytes, BodyString, QueryValues, Cookie, Cookies, SetContext, and SetPath.

Binding And Validation

Zinc’s default binder can combine path, query, and request-body data into one struct. If a Validator is configured, validation runs automatically after binding. 

type CreateUserInput struct {
    TeamID int    `path:"teamID"`
    Page   int    `query:"page"`
    Name   string `json:"name"`
    Auth   string `header:"x-auth"`
}

app.Post("/teams/:teamID/users", func(c *zinc.Context) error {
    var input CreateUserInput
    if err := c.Bind(&input); err != nil {
        return err
    }

    return c.Status(zinc.StatusCreated).JSON(input)
})

Narrower helpers are available too: 

c.BindJSON(&input)
c.BindXML(&input)
c.BindForm(&input)
c.BindQuery(&input)
c.BindHeader(&input)
c.BindPath(&input)

Multipart helpers are exposed directly on the context: FormFile, FormFiles, MultipartForm, and SaveFile.

Responses

Response helpers always return error. Once a response has been written, later writes return ErrResponseAlreadySent. 

app.Get("/text", func(c *zinc.Context) error {
    return c.String("plain text")
})

app.Get("/json", func(c *zinc.Context) error {
    return c.JSON(zinc.Map{"ok": true})
})

app.Get("/pretty", func(c *zinc.Context) error {
    return c.JSONPretty(zinc.Map{"ok": true}, "  ")
})

app.Get("/xml", func(c *zinc.Context) error {
    return c.XML(struct {
        Value string `xml:"value"`
    }{Value: "x"})
})

app.Get("/stream", func(c *zinc.Context) error {
    return c.Stream("text/plain", strings.NewReader("hello"))
})

app.Get("/redirect", func(c *zinc.Context) error {
    return c.Redirect(http.StatusMovedPermanently, "/new-home")
})

app.Get("/render", func(c *zinc.Context) error {
    return c.Render("home", zinc.Map{"Title": "Dashboard"})
})

app.Get("/empty", func(c *zinc.Context) error {
    return c.Status(zinc.StatusNoContent).NoContent()
})

Render requires a Renderer to be configured in Config. When no renderer is configured, Zinc returns an error instead of guessing.

Real-Time: SSE And WebSockets

Zinc keeps real-time support compact: use SSE for one-way server push and WS for bidirectional sockets. Both are first-class route helpers and can also be used from grouped routes. 

app.SSE("/events", func(c *zinc.Context, stream *zinc.SSEStream) error {
    ticker := time.NewTicker(time.Second)
    defer ticker.Stop()

    for {
        select {
        case <-stream.Done():
            return nil
        case tick := <-ticker.C:
            if err := stream.Send(zinc.SSEEvent{
                Event: "tick",
                Data: zinc.Map{"at": tick.UTC().Format(time.RFC3339)},
            }); err != nil {
                return err
            }
        }
    }
})

app.WS("/ws", func(c *zinc.Context, conn *websocket.Conn) error {
    for {
        messageType, payload, err := conn.ReadMessage()
        if err != nil {
            return nil
        }
        if err := conn.WriteMessage(messageType, payload); err != nil {
            return err
        }
    }
}, zinc.WebSocketConfig{
    CheckOrigin: func(c *zinc.Context) bool {
        return c.GetHeader(zinc.HeaderOrigin) == "http://localhost:3000"
    },
})

Plain browser clients work directly, and frameworks like React, Next.js, and Vue use the same browser APIs: 

<script>
  const events = new EventSource("/events");
  events.addEventListener("tick", (event) => {
    console.log("sse", JSON.parse(event.data));
  });

  const ws = new WebSocket("ws://localhost:8080/ws");
  ws.onopen = () => ws.send("hello");
  ws.onmessage = (event) => console.log("ws", event.data);
</script>

Files, Static Assets, And Mounted Handlers

Zinc can serve static directories, individual files, file-system backed files, and mounted net/http handlers. 

app.Static("/assets", "./public")
app.File("/robots.txt", "./public/robots.txt")

fsys := os.DirFS("./fixtures")
app.FileFS("/download", "report.txt", fsys)

app.Get("/attachment", func(c *zinc.Context) error {
    return c.Attachment("./public/report.txt", "report.txt")
})

admin := http.NewServeMux()
admin.HandleFunc("/health", func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
    _, _ = w.Write([]byte("ok"))
})
app.Mount("/admin", admin)

app.Get("/legacy", zinc.WrapFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
    _, _ = w.Write([]byte("legacy"))
}))

Configuration And Errors

Config controls routing behavior, body limits, server timeouts, trust-proxy behavior, and the extension interfaces Zinc uses for binding, validation, rendering, JSON encoding, and error translation. 

app := zinc.NewWithConfig(zinc.Config{
    ServerHeader:           "zinc/example",
    CaseSensitive:          true,
    StrictRouting:          true,
    AutoHead:               true,
    AutoOptions:            true,
    HandleMethodNotAllowed: true,
    BodyLimit:              8 << 20,
    ProxyHeader:            zinc.HeaderXForwardedFor,
    TrustedProxies:         []string{"10.0.0.1"},
    ErrorHandler: func(c *zinc.Context, err error) {
        var httpErr *zinc.HTTPError
        if errors.As(err, &httpErr) {
            _ = c.Status(httpErr.Code).String(httpErr.Error())
            return
        }
        _ = c.Status(zinc.StatusInternalServerError).String("internal server error")
    },
})

Returning a plain error yields a 500 from the default error handler. Returning a HTTPError lets you set a specific status code and message. 

app.Get("/bad-request", func(c *zinc.Context) error {
    return zinc.NewError(zinc.StatusBadRequest).WithMessage("name is required")
})

Route Introspection

Zinc can report registered routes for tooling, admin surfaces, or debugging. 

for _, route := range app.Routes() {
    log.Printf("%s %s -> %s", route.Method, route.Path, route.Handler)
}

Optional Middleware Packages

Focused middleware can live outside the core. Zinc ships a CORS middleware package: 

import zinccors "github.com/0mjs/zinc/middleware/cors"

app.Use(zinccors.New())

// Or with options:
app.Use(zinccors.NewWithOptions(
    zinccors.WithAllowOrigins("https://example.com"),
    zinccors.WithAllowCredentials(true),
))
